meta.titre: The Nervous System: Neurones, Reflexes and the Brain
meta.sous_theme: Neurone structure, reflex arc and brain regions

sections.contenu_markdown: A cook at a roadside stall in Douala brushes her hand against a hot pot and pulls it away before she even feels pain. A moment later she notices the burn and decides to run cold water over it. Two different kinds of response have just happened, one automatic and one chosen. The GCE asks about the parts of a neurone, the path of a reflex and the work of each part of the brain, and sometimes asks you to draw and label the brain.

items: A stimulus is a change in the surroundings that can be detected.
Receptors detect stimuli and effectors, such as muscles and glands, carry out responses.
The brain is protected by the skull and the spinal cord by the vertebral column.

sections.titre: Neurones, reflexes and regions of the brain
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Organization
The **central nervous system** (CNS) is the brain and spinal cord. Nerves that run to and from the CNS form the peripheral nervous system. Messages travel along nerve cells (**neurones**) as electrical impulses.

### The neurone
| Part | Role |
|---|---|
| Cell body | Contains the nucleus and controls the cell |
| Dendrites | Short branches that receive impulses and carry them **towards** the cell body |
| Axon | Long fibre that carries impulses **away from** the cell body |
| Myelin sheath | Fatty covering that insulates many axons and speeds up the impulse |

There are three kinds: **sensory neurones** carry impulses from receptors to the CNS, **relay neurones** connect neurones inside the CNS, and **motor neurones** carry impulses from the CNS to effectors. Between two neurones lies a tiny gap, the **synapse**. A chemical released at the end of one neurone crosses the gap and starts an impulse in the next, so impulses cross a synapse in one direction only.

### The reflex arc
stimulus, receptor, sensory neurone, relay neurone in the spinal cord, motor neurone, effector, response. A **reflex action** is fast, automatic and protective, and it does not need thought.

### Regions of the brain
| Region | Main job |
|---|---|
| Cerebrum | Largest part. Voluntary actions, thinking, memory and understanding of sensations |
| Cerebellum | Balance and co-ordination of movement |
| Medulla oblongata | Controls breathing and heart rate. Joins the brain to the spinal cord |
| Hypothalamus | Controls body temperature |

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question follows an impulse after a stimulus
variantes.contenu_markdown: Give the sequence in order and name the type of neurone at each stage. The spinal cord acts as the coordinator, and the brain is not needed for the response itself. The brain learns about the event afterwards, which is why pain is felt late.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks you to compare two kinds of action
variantes.contenu_markdown: A reflex is automatic, fast and not decided by the brain, as when the hand is pulled away from a hot object. A voluntary action is chosen and controlled by the cerebrum, as when you write an answer.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When you are asked to draw and label the brain
variantes.contenu_markdown: Draw a large side view with a sharp pencil. The cerebrum is a big folded dome covering the top and front. The small cerebellum sits below it at the back. The medulla oblongata lies at the base and continues downwards as the spinal cord. Add the hypothalamus and the pituitary gland if you know them. Label with ruled lines that touch the part and never cross each other.

sections.enonce_markdown: A woman touches a hot cooking pot and her hand jerks away at once. Describe the pathway of the impulses and explain why she feels pain only afterwards.

etapes.action: Name the stimulus and the receptor.
etapes.justification: A reflex starts with a stimulus detected by a receptor.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The heat is the stimulus, detected by temperature and pain receptors in the skin.

etapes.action: Follow the impulse into the CNS.
etapes.justification: A sensory neurone carries impulses towards the CNS.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The sensory neurone carries the impulse to the spinal cord.

etapes.action: Show the connection inside the spinal cord.
etapes.justification: A relay neurone links the sensory and motor neurones across synapses.
etapes.resultat_markdown: A relay neurone passes the impulse on to a motor neurone.

etapes.action: Follow the impulse to the effector.
etapes.justification: A motor neurone carries impulses away from the CNS.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The motor neurone carries the impulse to muscles of the arm, which contract and pull the hand away.

etapes.action: Explain the delay in feeling pain.
etapes.justification: Impulses also travel up to the brain, which takes longer than the reflex pathway.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Impulses also reach the cerebrum, where pain is felt, after the hand has already moved.

sections.conclusion_markdown: **Model answer.** The heat stimulates receptors in the skin. A sensory neurone carries the impulse to the spinal cord. A relay neurone passes it to a motor neurone, which carries it to the muscles of the arm. The muscles are the effectors, and they contract and pull the hand away. This pathway does not need the brain, so it is quick. Impulses also travel to the cerebrum, so the woman feels pain a moment later.

items.erreur_markdown: Dendrites carry impulses away from the cell body.
items.pourquoi_faux: Dendrites receive impulses and carry them towards the cell body. The axon carries them away.
items.correction_markdown: Dendrites carry impulses towards the cell body. The axon carries them away from it.

items.erreur_markdown: The cerebellum is the part for thinking and memory, and the cerebrum controls balance.
items.correction_markdown: The cerebrum is for thinking, memory and voluntary actions. The cerebellum is for balance and coordination of movement.

items.erreur_markdown: In a reflex action the impulse must travel through the brain first.
items.pourquoi_faux: That would make the response slow. A reflex is processed in the spinal cord.
items.correction_markdown: The reflex arc passes through the spinal cord, and the brain is informed afterwards.

items.erreur_markdown: A synapse is a place where two neurones are joined into one continuous fibre.
items.pourquoi_faux: There is a small gap, and the message crosses it by a chemical.
items.correction_markdown: At a synapse a chemical crosses the gap between two neurones, and it moves in one direction only.

items.enonce_markdown: Name the part of the brain that (a) controls balance, (b) controls the breathing rate, (c) is responsible for thinking and memory.
Make a table to compare a reflex action with a voluntary action. Give one example of each.
items.solution_markdown:
| | Reflex action | Voluntary action |
|---|---|---|
| Control | Spinal cord (automatic) | Cerebrum (chosen) |
| Speed | Very fast | Slower |
| Purpose | Protects the body | Any deliberate act |
| Example | Pulling the hand off a hot object | Writing an answer in an examination |

items.enonce_markdown: A road accident damages (a) the cerebellum of one man and (b) the motor neurones that go to the leg muscles of another man, while his sensory neurones are fine. Predict what each patient will find difficult and explain.
items.solution_markdown: (a) The first man has trouble with **balance and smooth coordination**: he sways and walks unsteadily, because the cerebellum coordinates movement and balance. (b) The second man **feels touch on his leg but cannot move it**: sensory impulses still reach the CNS, but motor neurones carry impulses from the CNS to effectors, and with them damaged the leg muscles get no instructions.

items_markdown: Neurones have a cell body, dendrites (towards the cell body) and an axon (away from the cell body), and many axons have a myelin sheath.
Sensory neurones carry impulses to the CNS, relay neurones link neurones in it and motor neurones carry impulses to effectors.
The reflex arc: stimulus, receptor, sensory neurone, relay neurone, motor neurone, effector, response.
A reflex is quick, automatic and passes through the spinal cord, and a voluntary action is controlled by the cerebrum.
Cerebrum: thinking and voluntary actions. Cerebellum: balance. Medulla oblongata: breathing and heart rate. Hypothalamus: body temperature.
